For SPY (S&P 500 ETF), the mean t+1 return when the close is ABOVE its own trailing 50-day simple moving average is HIGHER than when it is below -- SMA_CROSSOVER(50) on SPY, 2024 full year. Direction INCREASE pre-declared on the trend-following prior (Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron 1992; Faber 2007: price above its own trailing average marks the regime that carries the positive drift). First Nivel 5 Hypothesis of the project (US equities, a market with overnight gaps, sessions and holidays that crypto does not have).

Window history, declared before execution: SMA(200) was run first on this exact instrument and period and returned INCONCLUSIVE -- SPY closed above its 200-day average on every trading day of 2024, leaving the lower group empty and the difference of means undefined. The window moved to 50 on that validity ground alone: an undefined comparison is not an unfavourable one, and no metric from that run existed to shop for. 50 is a window the cited literature itself tests (Brock et al. examine 1, 2, 5, 50, 150 and 200 day averages), not one selected here. Period, folds, direction and acceptance criterion are unchanged from the original pre-declaration.

Pre-declared caveats: (1) SPY SMA(50) is among the most widely known signals in finance and may be fully arbitraged; (2) 2024 was a strong bull year, so positive drift favours the INCREASE direction -- walk-forward consistency across sub-periods, not the full-sample mean, is the real test; (3) this is the second window tried on one period, and the result carries that.

For SPY, the mean t+1 return when close_t is ABOVE its own value 10 trading days earlier is LOWER than when it is at or below it. Direction DECREASE pre-declared on the SHORT-HORIZON REVERSAL prior (Jegadeesh 1990, monthly reversals; Lehmann 1990, weekly reversals): at daily-to-monthly horizons reversal dominates, while momentum proper is a 3-12 month phenomenon (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993), so a 10-day lookback against a 1-day forward return sits in the reversal regime, not the momentum one.

Pre-declared caveats: (1) The reversal literature is largely cross-sectional across many stocks; a single index ETF is a much weaker test of it. (2) This project's crypto evidence also showed reversal signs. That observation did NOT motivate this direction -- the Jegadeesh/Lehmann prior predates it and is independent -- but the coincidence is recorded rather than hidden. (3) Class balance risk: a lagged-close comparison skews upward in a trending year. Both states are expected to occur, but not evenly.

For SPY, the mean t+1 return when volume_t is ABOVE its own trailing 20-day average is HIGHER than when it is at or below it. Direction INCREASE pre-declared on the HIGH-VOLUME RETURN PREMIUM (Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin 2001): securities experiencing unusually high trading volume subsequently earn higher returns, attributed to the visibility such volume confers.

Pre-declared caveats: (1) The original premium is CROSS-SECTIONAL on individual stocks over 1-20 day horizons. Its transfer to a single broad-index ETF is not established and may not hold at all. (2) Volume for an ETF reflects creation/redemption and hedging flow as well as directional interest, so the mechanism may not be the one documented. (3) Class balance expected to be reasonable: volume mean-reverts around its own trailing average, so both states recur by construction.

For SPY, the mean t+1 return when the intraday range (high-low)/close is ABOVE its own trailing 20-day average is LOWER than when it is at or below it. Direction DECREASE pre-declared on the LOW-VOLATILITY ANOMALY (Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang 2006; Baker, Bradley & Wurgler 2011): high-volatility assets earn lower returns than the risk-return relation predicts, with realised intraday range standing in for realised volatility.

Pre-declared caveats: (1) The anomaly is documented CROSS-SECTIONALLY and at monthly horizons. A 1-day forward return on one ETF is a far weaker test, and the sign need not survive at that frequency. (2) Intraday range also spikes on news days, where the next-day return is dominated by the news rather than by any volatility premium. (3) Class balance expected to be reasonable: range mean-reverts around its own trailing average.

hypotheses.description:
For SPY, the mean t+1 return when close_t is ABOVE its trailing 10-day average AND volume_t is ABOVE its trailing 20-day average is HIGHER than otherwise. Direction INCREASE pre-declared on VOLUME AS CONFIRMATION (Blume, Easley & O'Hara 1994: volume carries information about the quality of a price signal that price alone does not), the formal basis for the practitioner premise that a price move on rising volume is more reliable than one without it.

Pre-declared caveats: (1) A conjunction is the highest class-imbalance risk in this batch: it can only shrink the UPPER group relative to either condition alone. It is expected to be dominated by the volume term, since close above a 10-day average is common. (2) Combining two signals that may individually carry no edge does not create one; this project already refuted a four-signal portfolio on those grounds. (3) Blume/Easley/O'Hara is a theoretical microstructure result, not a documented trading edge at daily frequency on an index ETF.

For a MARKET-NEUTRAL CARRY in BTC -- long BTC-USD spot, short the Hyperliquid perpetual at equal notional -- the mean forward carry return when funding is AT OR ABOVE zero is HIGHER than when it is below. Direction INCREASE pre-declared.

The outcome is NOT a price change: it is the funding received over the period MINUS the change in basis, a cash flow plus a spread mark. Measuring only the funding would describe a position that cannot lose, which is not the position held -- and would hide that a liquidation cascade, driving the perpetual below spot, is FAVOURABLE to the short leg.

WHAT THIS TESTS AND WHY: not whether the premium exists -- that is already measured, and is a level claim about one group that the M2.x apparatus structurally cannot express. It tests whether the EXIT RULE discriminates, which is a two-group comparison the apparatus judges natively, and which is the only thing the destination's clause 'stop when the evidence stops supporting it' rests on. Today that rule is a declared threshold nobody has tested.

THE THRESHOLD IS ZERO because it is the only parameter-free boundary: the point where the economics invert, from being paid to hold to paying to hold. Any other number would come from looking at the data first.

NO LOOKAHEAD: the row at t is classified by funding at t-1, never its own still-accruing rate, and the outcome reads funding at t+1. Signal and outcome are two periods apart and cannot overlap.

SINGLE VENUE: funding and perpetual both from Hyperliquid. Pairing one exchange's funding with another's price would compute a basis nobody could trade. That fixes the period -- 2024-2025 is the whole of what exists where both series are real.

Period role: IN SAMPLE. The claim survives only if the full-sample metric is POSITIVE in BOTH 2024 and 2025 -- one chance in four under the null. A negative metric in the out-of-sample year means the in-sample result is not reproducible and NO further period is tried; trying periods until one agrees is the failure this test exists to prevent. Walk-forward consistency is secondary evidence, reported but not decisive.

WHY A RELATIVE THRESHOLD AND NOT ZERO. The absolute version (Hypothesis #37) classifies by sign, and the inverted group holds 11 of 366 days in 2024 and 18 of 365 in 2025, with one walk-forward fold each year containing NONE -- so the validation can only answer INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, and more data never fixes it because the split is degenerate at any length. funding_rate_surge_strategy documented that exact failure for the funding signal in September and fixed it by comparing the series to its own history; this carries the fix across to the exit rule.
